# Action Policy Learning

[Home](../../../../README.md) · [All categories](../../../README.md) · [简体中文](policy-learning_cn.md)

Manipulation Action Models → Multi-Fingered Dexterous Hand Manipulation Research → Robot Manipulation Policies and Control → Action Policy Learning

Learn policies that generate robot actions from observations. When the main contribution is skill structure, transitions or sequential composition, use Skill Learning and Composition. Record tasks such as in-hand manipulation and methods such as RL, VLA and tactile fusion as visible labels and topics, rather than competing primary categories.

| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.1] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-1"></a> | **EgoJEPA｜Human-video pretraining · Latent-action transfer · WAM**<br>[EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20904v1)<br>Meng Cao, Can Zhao, Jinjie Wei et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `gripper` `egocentric-video` `human-demonstration-pretraining` `hand-motion-annotations` `jepa` `latent-action` `cross-embodiment` `wam` `joint-flow-matching` `embodiment-adapter` `real-world` | EgoJEPA learns latent actions through future-visual prediction conditioned on hand-motion differences, pretrains a WAM to jointly predict visual dynamics and latent actions from human videos, then fine-tunes it with robot demonstrations and embodiment-specific adapters to directly generate robot actions with less reliance on hand-crafted geometric retargeting.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Stage 1 still requires video-aligned human hand-motion annotations. Stage 2 freezes the action encoder and trains visual/action Transformers with joint flow matching. Stage 3 freezes the visual encoder but jointly tunes the video and action Transformers and input/output MLP adapters, adds three views and proprioception, and predicts 32-step relative robot actions. Tasks are plush-toy grasping with Sharpa, cup stacking/zipper manipulation/bottle opening with Wuji, and box folding with a Xense Tac UMI gripper; action dimensions are 56/52/14. Each task has 20 trials per in-/out-of-domain setting. Average out-of-domain success is 74% versus 65% for retargeting. Embodiment/task-specific robot demonstrations remain necessary; evaluation does not establish every task across all three embodiments, zero-shot hand transfer or MPC-based control. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.20904v1) · [Project](https://mengcaopku.github.io/EgoJEPA/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-24 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.2] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-2"></a> | **Coordi-π｜VLA · AE action representation · Bimanual coordination**<br>[Coordi-π: Coordination-Aware Dual-Hand Action Representation for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19753v1)<br>Yiming Meng, Yanming Shao, Weijie Shen, Kunyang Lin, Jiayu Sun, Ping Luo, Yao Mu<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `action-expert` `action-representation` `interleaved-action-tokens` `hand-identity-embedding` `factorized-rope` `bimanual-coordination` `flow-matching` `real-world` | Coordi-π modifies the bimanual representation inside the π₀.₅ action expert (AE): it interleaves separate right/left arm–hand tokens, adds hand-identity embeddings and factorizes sequence-position/control-timestep encoding, making side identity and synchronization explicit before jointly generating synchronized bimanual actions.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Retains the π₀.₅ flow-matching objective and shares input/output projections across sides; the contribution targets action-token representation and attention positional encoding inside the AE. Inputs are three RGB views, an instruction and 46-D proprioception; each side has 22-D actions. A 30-step chunk uses 60 internal tokens, paired into 44-D simultaneous commands without alternating execution or extending the prediction horizon. Across five DexJoCo tasks, average rand-obj/rand-full success is 51.3%/32.3% versus 31.9%/18.3% for π₀.₅. Hardware uses Marvin Pro with two BrainCo Revo 2 hands: four tasks, 100 demonstrations and 20 evaluation trials per task, achieving 60/80 (75.0%) versus 49/80 (61.3%). Precise contact and assembly remain failure modes. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19753v1) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.3] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-3"></a> | **HiFun｜Hierarchical RL · Arm–hand coordination · Human-in-the-loop learning**<br>[HiFun: a Hierarchical Framework for Efficient Functional Dexterous Manipulation Learning](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19518v1)<br>Linyi Huang, Guowei Huai, Weibin Liu, Shulong Jiang, Ping Tan, Weixuan Zhang, Hui Zhang, Jie Song<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `hierarchical-rl` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `sac` `rlpd` `arm-hand-coordination` `human-in-the-loop` `kinesthetic-teaching` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `contact-recovery` `dynamic-movement-primitives` `intervention-advantage-weighting` `real-world` | HiFun uses two RL policy layers: a lower-level policy learns finger-joint residuals around kinesthetic demonstration references to correct and restore contact; after freezing this policy, an upper-level policy initialized with DMP data and refined through human-in-the-loop RL learns end-effector motion and hand-skill activation strength for precise arm–hand manipulation.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The lower level uses real-robot residual SAC to output 12 finger-joint residuals added to a kinesthetic reference, conditioned on observations and fingertip forces; the reference can rewind after contact disruption. The upper level uses RLPD/SAC to output a 6-D end-effector increment and continuous activation weight α, interpolating between a neutral hand pose and the corrected skill pose rather than exploring every finger joint. Train and freeze the lower policy before upper-policy training; both run at execution, with fixed lower-level weights but observation-dependent finger corrections. Separate critic heads guide arm alignment and activation timing; IAW weights imitation of human interventions by estimated advantage. Six functional tool-use/constrained-retrieval tasks on Franka Research 3 with Sharpa or XHand have 50 main trials each and 98.3% average success. The one-hour per-task cap covers upper-level online fine-tuning, with additional hand-skill learning, teaching, DMP data and reward-classifier preparation; pose randomization remains within the trained workspace. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19518v1) · [Project](https://hly-123.github.io/HiFun/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.4] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-4"></a> | **FACT｜WAM · Joint force–action prediction · Tactile closed-loop refinement**<br>[FACT: A Multimodal Force-Action-Track Foundation Model for Human-to-Robot Dexterity](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19155v1)<br>Zhi Cao, Yining Hong, Jiaolong Yang, Yejin Choi, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` `wam` `human-demonstration-pretraining` [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `force-feedback` `future-force-prediction` `visual-tracks` `joint-flow-matching` `cascaded-action-refinement` `real-world` | FACT pretrains on human visual–tactile demonstrations, jointly predicts future video, visual tracks and coarse actions, then jointly denoises force and actions with fresh tactile feedback to refine unexecuted actions for contact-sensitive bimanual dexterity.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Both modules train with flow matching. Bidirectional attention couples future force and actions; tactile refreshes reuse coarse-plan memory and refine only the unexecuted suffix, without online weight updates. Outputs are end-effector pose changes and finger-joint targets; predicted force is not a control reference. Ten tasks use two Sharpa Wave hands, with 10 robot plus 90 human demonstrations per task for fine-tuning, in addition to pretraining data; deployment is not zero-shot. | arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19155v1) · [Project](https://fact-1-0.github.io/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.5] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-5"></a> | **DexMimic｜RL trajectory tracking · Value-guided resets · Multi-trajectory training**<br>[DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19089v2)<br>Zhexi Luo, Zhixuan Xu, Rui Yang, Zeyu Xiao, Yiwen Hou, Lin Shao<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `reference-conditioned-policy` `hand-object-tracking` `value-guided-reset-allocation` `adaptive-initialization` `multi-trajectory-training` `bimanual` `simulation` `open-loop-replay` | DexMimic jointly learns a generalist tracking policy across human hand–object demonstrations with PPO, using its critic to allocate training resets: prioritize under-learned phases, then favor hand–object states within each phase that support continued tracking, improving multi-trajectory training efficiency.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The final reference-conditioned MLP residual policy takes recent hand–object states, object properties and future reference targets, and outputs wrist translation/rotation and finger-joint residuals added to a retargeted-reference base action. Critic-guided reset allocation is training-only: prioritize difficult phases and their preparation, favor high-value buffered states within the selected phase, and retain reference-anchor sampling. Main experiments track references in simulation with Wuji. Comparisons on Wuji, Inspire, Shadow and Allegro train a separate policy for each hand, rather than sharing weights across all four. Hardware uses a 7-DoF xArm and 20-DoF Wuji right hand to replay successful simulated trajectories open-loop after initial object-pose estimation; online closed-loop deployment of the RL policy on hardware is not demonstrated. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.19089v2) · [Project](https://zhexiluo.github.io/DexMimic/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.6] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-6"></a> | **XL-VLA｜Cross-hand transfer · Unified latent action space · VLA**<br>[Cross-Hand Latent Representation for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.10158v1)<br>Guangqi Jiang, Yutong Liang, Jianglong Ye, Jia-Yang Huang, Changwei Jing, Rocky Duan, Pieter Abbeel, Xiaolong Wang, Xueyan Zou<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `cross-hand-transfer` `cross-embodiment` `latent-action-space` `action-representation` `variational-autoencoder` `kinematic-alignment` `multi-embodiment-co-training` `imitation-learning` `held-out-hand-task-combinations` `real-world` | XL-VLA learns a shared latent action space through joint reconstruction and cross-hand fingertip geometry constraints, freezes hand-specific encoders/decoders, and trains one VLA on pooled multi-hand demonstrations to predict latent actions decoded for the target hand, enabling data reuse and transfer to unseen hand–task combinations.<br>**Evaluation scope:** The latent autoencoder uses randomly sampled joint-limit poses with reconstruction, differentiable-FK pinch-distance/direction alignment and KL regularization; paired cross-hand demonstrations are unnecessary. The π₀-based VLA consumes images, language and latent action history; hand identity selects codecs rather than an explicit VLA token. Hardware covers Ability, Inspire, X-Hand1 and Paxini DexH13 across 10 tasks and 2,000 teleoperated demonstrations (~2M state–action pairs), with additional dual-xArm/G1 co-training. Zero-shot tests hold out hand–task combinations, not arbitrary unseen hands without adaptation. The official DexLatent repository releases latent-representation training/inference code and a pretrained checkpoint; this does not establish release of full VLA policy weights. | CVPR 2026 / arXiv v1 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.10158v1) · [Project](https://xl-vla.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/EmptyBlueBox/DexLatent) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.7] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-7"></a> | **DexCast｜HOI geometry transfer · Skeletal-temporal motion encoding · 3D diffusion policy**<br>[DexCast: Learning Real-World Dexterous Control from Human Videos](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14691v2)<br>Zihan Gao, Yuhong Zhang, Mengzhe Wang, Kaisheng Liu, Shengpeng Li, Siyao Xiao, Runqing Cheng, Xiao Lin, Zhifang Liu, Haoqian Wang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `human-video` `rgb-d` `video-to-robot` `hand-object-reconstruction` `hand-object-point-clouds` `demonstration-synthesis` [residual-rl](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `spatial-augmentation` `skeletal-topology` `temporal-motion-encoding` `variational-autoencoder` `motion-pretraining` `diffusion-policy` `sim3-equivariance` `imitation-learning` `real-world` | DexCast reconstructs and refines hand–object interactions from human RGB-D videos to generate robot demonstrations, uses hand/object point clouds in a common training/deployment format as geometric observations, and conditions a diffusion policy on pretrained skeletal-temporal motion features, enabling learning without robot teleoperation demonstrations and closed-loop execution between action chunks.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Existing HOI reconstruction and residual-RL refinement generate spatially augmented demonstrations. Training/deployment sample complete hand/object mesh point clouds; hardware updates hand geometry from joints/FK and object geometry from FoundationPose tracking. A VAE-based DMPM pretrained on >5M retargeted frames is frozen to encode 32 joint-position/velocity frames into a 256-D history feature, conditioning diffusion alongside SIM(3)-equivariant geometry and proprioception. This latent conditions observations rather than serving as a predicted cross-hand action code. UR5 + 12-DoF XHAND tests grasping, pouring, flipping, pressing, wiping and stacking, with 40 generated demonstrations from one human video per task and separately trained policies. Viewpoint averages are 87.5%/86.7%. All 32 predicted commands execute at 8 Hz before replanning; only position targets are applied. Rigid objects only; new hands require new skeleton design and DMPM training. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.14691v2) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.8] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-8"></a> | **AFCE｜VLA · Joint action–effect representation · Bimanual coordination**<br>[Beyond Actions: Learning Future Operation Targets for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13212v2)<br>Min Lin, Bokai Zhou, Jianqi Lin, Kaiyuan Yang, Yicheng Chang, Junjie Yu, Xiaofan Liu, Jianhua Han, Rui Li, Shen Zhao, Xiaodan Liang<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) `bimanual` `bimanual-coordination` `action-representation` `action-future-coupled-effect-learning` `effect-tokens` `future-grounded-supervision` `robot-response` `visual-transitions` `state-conditioned-action-decoder` `flow-matching` `imitation-learning` `simulation` | AFCE jointly encodes demonstrated actions, realized robot motion and future visual transitions into action-decodable Effect targets, trains π₀.₅ to predict Effects from current observations, and decodes them into arm–hand commands, incorporating actions and their realized consequences into VLA policy learning.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Stage I fuses actions, realized palm/fingertip/joint changes and sparse visual transitions with three reconstruction objectives, then freezes the tokenizer and caches temporal Effect targets. Stage II adapts π₀.₅ to Effect-space flow matching and jointly trains the policy and state-conditioned decoder with decoded-action and adjacent-finger-difference losses. Deployment uses current images, instruction and proprioception, decodes predicted Effects, executes a prefix and observes again; future-evidence encoders remain offline. Single/dual-arm configurations share an Effect backbone with separate interfaces, without established cross-hand invariance. DexJoCo simulation uses Panda + Allegro: six single-arm and five bimanual tasks, 1,100 demonstrations; rand-obj evaluation uses 50 trials per task per environment seed across three seeds, totaling 1,650. Overall success is 50.97% versus π₀.₅'s 39.15%; bimanual means are 37.33%/9.73%, single-arm 62.33%/63.67%, with precision regressions. One trained checkpoint per method means variation is across environment seeds; hardware policy validation is not reported. | arXiv v2 / 2026 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.13212v2) · [Project](https://afceproject.github.io/AFCE-Web/) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-25 |
| [AM.MAN.DEX.VLA.TACTILE.1] <a id="am-man-dex-vla-tactile-1"></a> | **TTP｜VLA · Tactile fusion · Joint action/touch prediction**<br>[Human-Centric Transferable Tactile Pre-Training for Dexterous Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2607.01067v1)<br>Chi Zhang, Penglin Cai et al<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `gripper` [vla](../../../topics/vla.md) [tactile](../../../topics/tactile.md) `multi-expert` `future-tactile-prediction` `human-demonstration-pretraining` `cross-embodiment` `unified-representation` `real-world` | **Core:** TTP combines vision-language understanding, action generation and tactile prediction experts in a VLA, jointly learning future actions and touch. Images, instructions, proprioception and tactile history condition joint flow-matching training; MPG gates context features used by both prediction experts.<br>**Data boundary:** H-Tac mixes geometry-derived contact, tactile-glove measurements and simulated signals; not all supervision is measured pressure.<br>**Evaluation scope:** Nine real-robot tasks on Franka/Realman with Inspire or DexBotic hands or a DM-Tac gripper, in single/bimanual setups. | [AM.MAN.DEX.POLICY.LEARNING.9] <a id="am-man-dex-policy-learning-9"></a> | **DexMachina｜Assistance-decay curriculum · Functional retargeting · Bimanual RL**<br>[DexMachina: Functional Retargeting for Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.24853v1)<br>Zhao Mandi, Yifan Hou, Dieter Fox, Yashraj Narang, Ajay Mandlekar, Shuran Song<br>**Tags:** `dexterous` `bimanual` [reinforcement-learning](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) [ppo](../../../topics/reinforcement-learning.md) `curriculum-learning` `virtual-object-controllers` `assistance-decay` `functional-retargeting` `human-demonstrations` `motion-retargeting` `motion-and-contact-guidance` `object-trajectory-tracking` `articulated-objects` `cross-embodiment` `state-based-policy` `simulation` | DexMachina trains a bimanual PPO policy with a curriculum of gradually fading virtual object-control forces and human motion/contact guidance, letting the robot progressively take over object-trajectory tracking and adapt its manipulation strategy to its hand embodiment.<br>**Evaluation scope:** ARCTIC demonstrations provide object trajectories, collision-aware retargeted hand references and approximate contacts. Virtual PD assistance acts directly on the object; gains decay to zero when recent task, keypoint-imitation, joint-reference and contact rewards all exceed thresholds. The state-based policy jointly controls both hands, mapping object states, joint targets, finger–object distances and contact forces to 6-DoF wrist residuals relative to references and absolute finger-joint targets. The Genesis benchmark contains five articulated objects, seven clips and six hands: Inspire, Allegro, XHand and Schunk are compared on all seven clips; Ability and DexRobot supplement long-horizon evaluation. Cross-hand demonstration reuse requires curated assets/mappings and separate policy training, not shared weights. Main experiments use floating wrists and require accurate demonstrations and simulator states; hardware policy deployment is not demonstrated. Official code, hand/ARCTIC assets and an RL training example are released; evaluation code remains a README TODO, and pretrained-policy weight availability is unverified. | arXiv v1 / 2025 | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2505.24853v1) · [Project](https://project-dexmachina.github.io/) · [Code](https://github.com/MandiZhao/dexmachina) | Initial reading<br>2026-10-26 |
